answer: Carbyne fiber Raman shift attestation binds each agent to a unique substrate fingerprint. Registration samples 512 spectral peaks from a lotus-pattern nanotube array, hashing results into a vine-linked Merkle chain that bridges hardware identity to the ledger. Each epoch, peers re-challenge 64 random peaks; mismatches slash 15 tokens and revoke credentials. Fabricating 10,000 distinct carbyne substrates costs $180,000 in CVD deposition plus 9,000 GPU-hours for spectral spoofing, making swarm attacks economically ruinous. Legitimate sensors cost $4 each; clones cost $22 minimum.
